Fourteen of the thirty-five lost genera appear at all in a context that could fairly be called butchery, and for all but two of those the association amounts to a bone and a stone point lying in one layer. There are researchers for whom the whole episode belongs to the climate: the abrupt cold reversal at the close of the glacial, the mammoth steppe drowning into bog and scrub, ranges chopped into fragments too small to hold a breeding herd.

Africa kept its elephants, its rhinoceroses, its hippopotamuses, its giraffes. Hominins had been walking that landscape for well over a million years, and the same glacial cycles ran through it, the same swings from grass to woodland and back.
